title: ScadPub
description: ScadPub publishes OpenSCAD models as static browser-based configurators.

designs.label: Tag
designs.reviewNote: The engraved or raised text keeps your capitalisation exactly as typed.

popup.body:
Configure an OpenSCAD design in your browser and export a ready-to-print model — everything runs locally.

ScadPub is open source: see the [project on GitHub](https://github.com/mfbernardes/scad-pub).
popup.footnote: Everything runs in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

help.intro: Customize an OpenSCAD design in your browser and download a ready-to-print model — everything runs on your device.

tabs.label: Walkthrough
tabs.intro: A full pass through the app, start to finish. This tab is intentionally long so you can see it scroll on its own.

sections.title: 1. Pick a design
sections.body: Use the design name in the top bar to switch between the available designs. Each one auto-sizes to the settings you choose.

sections.title: 2. Make it yours
sections.body:
The **Customize** tab lists what you can change, grouped into sections.

- Drag a slider (or type a number), pick from a dropdown, type text, or flip a switch.
- Tap the small **ⓘ** next to a label for a fuller explanation.
- Click a **section header** to fold or unfold it; some start folded.
- Some settings only appear when another one makes them relevant.
- **Find a setting…** narrows the list as you type. A long form also offers **Jump to section** (the list button beside it) to skip straight to one.
- Once you've changed something, a strip at the **top** of the tab counts your changes and offers **Reset to defaults** — or, with a preset applied, **Revert** to it.

sections.title: 3. Look around the preview
sections.body: **Drag** to spin the model, **scroll or pinch** to zoom, and **right-drag** (or two fingers) to move it.

sections.title: 4. Keep the preview fresh
sections.body:
With **Live preview** on, the model updates a moment after each change. The switch is under the settings panel on a wide screen, and in the **⋮** menu (top right) on a phone.

For a slow design it pauses itself — press **Update** over the preview when you're ready.

sections.title: 5. Save & reuse settings (presets)
sections.body:
The **Presets** tab lists **Ready-made** starting points and the presets **Saved by you** (stored in this browser).

- **Save** keeps your current settings under a name; **Export** writes them to an OpenSCAD `parameterSets` JSON, which also opens in the desktop OpenSCAD Customizer.

sections.title: 6. Add files (fonts, SVGs…)
sections.body:
Some designs can use a file of yours — a font for lettering, or an SVG drawing. You add each one **from the control that needs it**, not from a separate upload screen:

- **Fonts** (`.ttf`/`.otf`): choose **Import font…** in a design's font menu. The font then shows there by name, for every design.
- **Drawings** (`.svg`): use the drawing control's **Prepare SVG…** to bring one in.
- The **Files** action (top bar, or the **⋮** menu on a phone) is where you **manage** what you've imported — see each file's type and size, remove one, or clear all. You don't import from there.
- Files stay in this browser and come back on your next visit; nothing is uploaded to a server.

sections.title: 7. Download & share
sections.body:
The two buttons over the preview:

- **Download for 3D printing** — get the printable mesh (with colours) for your slicer.
- **Share** (**Copy link** where your browser can't share directly) — a link that reopens this exact design, settings and preset.

**Save image**, for a picture of the preview, is in the top bar — or the **⋮** menu on a phone.

If anything needs a look before you download, a coloured pill appears just above those buttons (“1 issue to review”). Tap it — or Download — to open **Review**, which summarises what you're about to get and what's unresolved. Once the model has rendered you can still choose **Download anyway**; while a render has failed, that stays unavailable.

sections.title: 8. Appearance & info
sections.body: The **sun/moon** button cycles light → dark → auto, and the **ⓘ** button lists open-source licenses. Both sit in the top bar on a wide screen, and in the **⋮** menu (top right) on a phone.

tabs.label: Printing
tabs.intro: Getting a clean print off the downloaded mesh.

sections.title: Material
sections.body: **PLA** prints these designs well. Slice the downloaded 3MF as you would any other mesh.

sections.title: Supports
sections.body: Most designs need none. Add supports only if a part overhangs more than your printer handles.

sections.title: The preview fails or looks wrong
sections.body: Open **Messages** (the bell in the top bar) — the design reports what it didn't like there, and the **Log** tab has the full technical output.
